notes: Lantern: moth-folk, Concord pilots by tradition; a FLOATING rig when gliding (kind "floating": 49x49, pivot (24,24)). Dusty wings folded on the back like a swept tent with a swallow-tail, a fuzzy cream ruff, big dark compound eyes and feathery antennae; the body is the normal body in the middle of the frame (the drawer bobs it). The legs layer is what hangs behind it: thin legs under the swallow-tail and a pair of wing tips that open and close at the sides (`float`: 6 frames, 6 fps, played by time; `stand`: wings folded). The mounts are the human's moved by (+8,+8). torso_glow (2 pulse frames at ~2 fps) lights the wings' eye-spots, head_glow the antenna lamps. Head variants: antennae (default), goggles (tinted frames, blue glass), helmet (a tinted leather cap, antennae out through slits). Outfit mask = the pilot's scarf, the goggle frames and the cap. Same rig as human: every layer faces UP at rotation 0 on one 49x49 frame, rotate about the pivot; outfit pixels are neutral grey in the base PNG and white in *_color.png (multiply by the outfit colour there); no baked shadow.

legs.notes: frames 0-5 are the float cycle (a closed loop played by time, whether or not they move), frame 6 the idle: this layer is what trails behind the body (drawn pointing back, turned to the movement direction)

arms.notes: item placement: item top-left = mount - item.grip (both unrotated), then rotate the upper group about the pivot. Mounts are identical on every species (and the human), so any item fits any body. Pose = the item's class: pistol, rifle, tool, heavy, melee. RIG KIND floating: this frame is 49x49 with the pivot at (24,24), so every mount here is the shared one moved by (+8,+8): mount - pivot is identical to the human rig.

glow.notes: per head variant, a list of glow frames: alternate them at 2 fps
